name: Suvorexant

lead: Suvorexant (Belsomra) is a prescription insomnia drug approved in 2014 that blocks the brain's wake-promoting orexin signals.
Trials support effects on falling and staying asleep; no studies link it to appearance outcomes.

paras: It competitively blocks orexin A and B at OX1 and OX2 receptors, reducing arousal rather than broadly depressing the central nervous system through GABA.
Next-day somnolence, headache and dizziness are reported, with rare complex sleep behaviours. It is Schedule IV in the US and interacts with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and alcohol.

lead: Suvorexant is a dual orexin receptor antagonist developed by Merck and sold as Belsomra. The US FDA approved it in August 2014 as the first drug of its class for insomnia characterised by difficulty with sleep onset and/or maintenance [1]. It blocks orexin A and B at OX1 and OX2 receptors, reducing wake-promoting signalling rather than acting through GABA [1][2].
It is Schedule IV in the US [1]. No study has examined it for appearance, and no looksmaxxing community discussion was identified.
Randomised trials, including a one-year trial, reported improvements in sleep latency and wake time with next-day somnolence among reported effects [3][4][5].

paras: Suvorexant is indicated for adults with insomnia [1]. The 2017 AASM guideline and the 2022 Lancet network meta-analysis include it among insomnia medications, with the guideline recommending it for sleep onset and maintenance [6][7]. A 2024 trial reported less postoperative delirium with suvorexant after cardiac surgery in older adults [1].

Next-day somnolence, headache and dizziness are common; complex sleep behaviours have been reported rarely [1]. Concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated and alcohol adds to sedation [1]. Its Schedule IV status reflects abuse potential [1].

Suvorexant competitively blocks both orexin receptors [1][8]. A 2015 Nature paper described the crystal structure of the human OX2 receptor bound to suvorexant [9], and a 2011 paper described its sleep-promoting effects in preclinical work [10].

A phase 3 trial in The Lancet Neurology followed insomnia patients for one year, with abrupt discontinuation after [3]. A 2012 Neurology randomised trial and two three-month trials in Biological Psychiatry tested it against placebo [4][5]. Registered studies examined hepatic and renal impairment and its use in opioid and alcohol use disorders [11][12]. No studies were found on suvorexant for appearance outcomes.

timeline.event: FDA approves Belsomra, the first orexin receptor antagonist [1].
Crystal structure of OX2 receptor bound to suvorexant published [9].
